After the statement, technology was still the leading gainer and energy was still the biggest loser. Investors will be watching Warsh's press conference for more details on the Fed's thinking.

"Warsh not only read the markets, but he read the room, supporting a rate hike. That’s why we can get a relatively muted response from the markets despite the change in course," said Brian Jacobsen, chief economic strategist at Annex Wealth Management.
But Jacobsen said in an email that he "wouldn’t bank on another hike this year."
"Yes, the median dot shows another hike this year, but a lot can change between now and then," he said.
